+
+# Sprite-sheet authoring
+
+Use this skill when adding or replacing a raster sprite in an atlas, updating
+an atlas manifest, or producing a companion map for an atlas. It is especially
+useful for class emblems and other fixed-cell game art.
+
+## Do not assume a companion map
+
+First inspect the asset contract. A sprite sheet may have:
+
+- only a color/albedo atlas;
+- a color atlas plus a tangent-space normal atlas; or
+- a true UV/layout map used by a shader or mesh pipeline.
+
+These are different artifacts. Do not generate a normal map or call it a UV
+map unless the consuming code and existing assets establish that convention.
+
+## Safe atlas workflow
+
+1. Inspect the existing atlas dimensions, alpha mode, cell size, manifest, and
+   any companion maps before editing.
+2. Generate the new sprite as a transparent standalone image, then normalize
+   it into the target cell without changing neighboring cells.
+3. Use the deterministic helper in `scripts/atlas_tool.py` for inspection,
+   cell insertion, and optional normal-map generation.
+4. Prefer PNG as the compositing/intermediate format for alpha-sensitive work.
+   WebP is not inherently wrong, but re-encoding an existing transparent WebP
+   can change premultiplied RGB in fully transparent pixels or expose encoder
+   artifacts. Preserve the original WebP unless the output is decoded and
+   visually checked; switching the manifest to a validated PNG atlas is safer
+   than shipping damaged alpha.
+5. Update the manifest only after the atlas cell is validated. Keep color and
+   companion-map coordinates identical.
+6. Validate with `view_image`, the helper's `inspect` command, and the smallest
